From ea55c65dedf40e9c1911dc1e63e26bc9a59692b9 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Jonas Gorski <jonas.gorski@gmail.com>
Date: Thu, 6 Jun 2024 12:56:33 -0700
Subject: [PATCH] serial: bcm63xx-uart: fix tx after conversion to
 uart_port_tx_limited()

When bcm63xx-uart was converted to uart_port_tx_limited(), it implicitly
added a call to stop_tx(). This causes garbage to be put out on the
serial console. To fix this, pass UART_TX_NOSTOP in flags, and manually
call stop_tx() ourselves analogue to how a similar issue was fixed in
commit 7be50f2e8f20 ("serial: mxs-auart: fix tx").

Fixes: d11cc8c3c4b6 ("tty: serial: use uart_port_tx_limited()")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Jonas Gorski <jonas.gorski@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Doug Brown <doug@schmorgal.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20240606195632.173255-4-doug@schmorgal.com
Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>

diff --git a/drivers/tty/serial/bcm63xx_uart.c b/drivers/tty/serial/bcm63xx_uart.c
index 34801a6f300b..b88cc28c94e3 100644
--- a/drivers/tty/serial/bcm63xx_uart.c
+++ b/drivers/tty/serial/bcm63xx_uart.c
@@ -308,8 +308,8 @@ static void bcm_uart_do_tx(struct uart_port *port)
 
 	val = bcm_uart_readl(port, UART_MCTL_REG);
 	val = (val & UART_MCTL_TXFIFOFILL_MASK) >> UART_MCTL_TXFIFOFILL_SHIFT;
-
-	pending = uart_port_tx_limited(port, ch, port->fifosize - val,
+	pending = uart_port_tx_limited_flags(port, ch, UART_TX_NOSTOP,
+		port->fifosize - val,
 		true,
 		bcm_uart_writel(port, ch, UART_FIFO_REG),
 		({}));
@@ -320,6 +320,9 @@ static void bcm_uart_do_tx(struct uart_port *port)
 	val = bcm_uart_readl(port, UART_IR_REG);
 	val &= ~UART_TX_INT_MASK;
 	bcm_uart_writel(port, val, UART_IR_REG);
+
+	if (uart_tx_stopped(port))
+		bcm_uart_stop_tx(port);
 }
 
 /*
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `drivers/tty/serial/bcm63xx_uart.c`**
1. **Line Change**: The function call to `uart_port_tx_limited()` has been replaced with `uart_port_tx_limited_flags()`, which now includes the flag `UART_TX_NOSTOP`.
2. **Manual Stop Transmission**: After the transmission logic, a check for `uart_tx_stopped(port)` is added, and if true, it manually calls `bcm_uart_stop_tx(port)` to stop the transmission.

### Relationships Between Modifications
The modification addresses a bug introduced when the function was converted to use `uart_port_tx_limited()`, which implicitly called `stop_tx()`, leading to incorrect behavior (garbage output). By passing `UART_TX_NOSTOP` as a flag, the patch ensures that the transmission does not stop automatically, and the manual call to `bcm_uart_stop_tx(port)` ensures proper control over the transmission state, similar to a previous fix in another commit. This relationship highlights the need for careful management of transmission states when modifying low-level serial communication functions.

serial: bcm63xx-uart: fix tx after conversion to
 uart_port_tx_limited()

When bcm63xx-uart was converted to uart_port_tx_limited(), it implicitly
added a call to stop_tx(). This causes garbage to be put out on the
serial console. To fix this, pass UART_TX_NOSTOP in flags, and manually
call stop_tx() ourselves analogue to how a similar issue was fixed in
commit 7be50f2e8f20 ("serial: mxs-auart: fix tx").

Fixes: d11cc8c3c4b6 ("tty: serial: use uart_port_tx_limited()")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Jonas Gorski <jonas.gorski@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Doug Brown <doug@schmorgal.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20240606195632.173255-4-doug@schmorgal.com
Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>

Here is the root cause:
The bug was caused by the implicit call to `stop_tx()` when the `bcm63xx-uart` driver was converted to use `uart_port_tx_limited()`. This led to the transmission being stopped unexpectedly, resulting in garbage data being sent to the serial console. The fix involved passing the `UART_TX_NOSTOP` flag to prevent this automatic stopping behavior and manually controlling the transmission state.

Here is the patch:
  */
 static void bcm_uart_do_tx(struct uart_port *port)
 {
 	unsigned int val;
 	bool pending;
 	u8 ch;
 
 	val = bcm_uart_readl(port, UART_MCTL_REG);
 	val = (val & UART_MCTL_TXFIFOFILL_MASK) >> UART_MCTL_TXFIFOFILL_SHIFT;
-
-	pending = uart_port_tx_limited(port, ch, port->fifosize - val,
+	pending = uart_port_tx_limited_flags(port, ch, UART_TX_NOSTOP,
+		port->fifosize - val,
 		true,
 		bcm_uart_writel(port, ch, UART_FIFO_REG),
 		({}));
 	if (pending)
 		return;
 
 	/* nothing to send, disable transmit interrupt */
 	val = bcm_uart_readl(port, UART_IR_REG);
 	val &= ~UART_TX_INT_MASK;
 	bcm_uart_writel(port, val, UART_IR_REG);
+
+	if (uart_tx_stopped(port))
+		bcm_uart_stop_tx(port);
 }

Reason:
The call to `uart_port_tx_limited()` implicitly invokes `stop_tx()`, which stops the transmission unexpectedly. This results in garbage data being sent to the serial console because the transmission is halted before it can complete.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
pending = uart_port_tx_limited_flags(port, ch, UART_TX_NOSTOP, port->fifosize - val, true, bcm_uart_writel(port, ch, UART_FIFO_REG), ({}));
```
```c

    bcm_uart_stop_tx(port);
```
Reason:
By passing the `UART_TX_NOSTOP` flag to `uart_port_tx_limited_flags()`, the automatic stopping behavior is prevented, allowing the transmission to continue as intended. Additionally, the manual call to `bcm_uart_stop_tx(port)` ensures that the transmission can be stopped only when necessary, thus preventing the unintended transmission of garbage data.
